title: Raksha Kendra Offline Disaster & AI Lexicon
description: Critical emergency dictionary for weak-connectivity and offline civil defense operations

terms.definition: Sorting of patients into priority categories (Immediate/Red, Delayed/Yellow, Minimal/Green, Expectant/Black) to maximize survival when medical resources are limited.
Polyvalent serum effective against bites of the 'Big Four' venomous Indian snakes: Russell's Viper, Saw-scaled Viper, Spectacled Cobra, and Common Krait.
Constricting band applied 2-3 inches above an extremity arterial bleeding wound (never over a joint) to stop life-threatening catastrophic hemorrhage. Mark exact application time on forehead.
Abnormal rise in sea level caused by low atmospheric pressure and cyclonic gale winds pushing seawater inland, threatening low-lying coastal hamlets.
Catastrophic release of water from a glacial lake dammed by moraine, generating violent flash floods and boulder torrents in Himalayan river valleys.
India's specialized central paramilitary force dedicated to disaster search, rescue, chemical-biological response, and flood extraction.
Odisha Disaster Rapid Action Force — elite state disaster response unit equipped for cyclone and flood extrications.
Command command-and-control facility established at national, state (1070), and district (1077) levels to direct disaster response.
Radio communications operating on amateur frequencies (e.g. 145.200 MHz FM, 7.080 MHz HF) that function reliably when cellular towers and the internet fail.
Standard earthquake safety drill: Drop to your hands and knees, cover your head and neck beneath a sturdy desk, and hold on until shaking stops.
Water purification method using direct UV sunlight on clear PET bottles for 6 hours to destroy microbial pathogens.
Water purification chemicals used in disaster zones. 1 tablet per 1 liter of clear water or 2 drops of 5% unscented household bleach, with a 30-minute contact time.
International emergency distress signal: 3 whistle blasts, 3 torch flashes, 3 smoke puffs, or 3 gunshots indicating an urgent plea for rescue.
Distress telegraphic code: 3 short pulses, 3 long pulses, 3 short pulses transmitted via flashlight, mirror, sound horn, or radio.
Dangerous drop in core body temperature below 35°C, common in wet flood environments. Treat by removing wet clothing, insulating with foil emergency blanket, and warm fluids.
